observations: An established diagnostic SSH session completed sleep 2 with guest CLOCK_START=1789826326 and CLOCK_END=1789826329; whole authenticated session took 48.0 seconds.

A separate workqueue trace instance recorded 176 entries without overwrite. Ten paired drm_fb_helper_damage_work calls spanned 4.048998 seconds within a five-second trace, maximum 0.600743 seconds. This is elapsed work duration, not measured CPU time. One start was unpaired at the end.
fb_flashcursor and virtio-gpu completion work interleaved with framebuffer damage work. The trace instance was removed after capture.
A reversible cursor-off experiment restored cursor_blink=1. Its strict SSH success (9.16 seconds) cannot be assigned to a cursor phase because host phase timing was insufficiently recorded.

Matched control: with cursor_blink=1 and one diagnostic SSH session held open for 90 seconds, a second SSH command using ServerAliveInterval=5 and ServerAliveCountMax=1 returned STRICT_SESSION_OK in 14.10 seconds.
The held session exited normally. After an additional 30-second host wait, the identical strict SSH command failed with exit 255 in 16.93 seconds: Timeout, server 127.0.0.1 not responding.

User-manager journal shows runtime-directory start 14:11:27 to 14:11:32 UTC, then user@1000.service start 14:11:33 to 14:11:53 UTC. This supports delayed cold session setup; it does not establish the cause of every earlier timeout.
source_finding: libvmm/src/virtio/gpu_2d.c backing_read scans entries from index zero for each transferred row. A monotonic bounded traversal is a candidate optimization, not yet implemented or qualified.
limitations: No qualification timeout, assertion or guest service policy changed.
Guest remains live; final harness exit still untested.
